messages.author: cf0a61b30321fbd5
messages.subject: Endotherm Stand Up
parts:
Hi Mike,

I am currently working on modelling a ground nesting bird whilst it is incubating and a key feature I want to include is the fact that birds can cool themselves down quite a bit by standing up. What would be the simplest way to implement incubating vs standing? I was going to keep all else equal bar the following :

Incubating
TAIR <- TAIR.10cm.50shd  # TA at 10cm
TGRD <- TGRD.50shd         # Ground temp
TCONDSB<-  TGRD.50shd   # Ground temp
SHAPE_MAX <- 2

Standing
TAIR <- TAIR.30cm.50shd  # TA at 30cm
TGRD <-  TAIR.10cm.50shd    # TA at 10cm
TCONDSB<-  TAIR.10cm.50shd  # TA at 10cm
SHAPE_MAX <- 4

Or should I simply keep TAIR, TGRD, TCONSDSB the same and have PCOND = 0.5 for incubating and PCOND = 0 for standing?

All the best,
Shane.

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Endotherm Stand Up
parts:
Hi Shane,
I'd definitely simulate the air temperature, wind speed and humidity at the two heights, i.e. the mid-point of the bird when sitting and standing, and then when it's sitting, and turn off conduction when they are standing and make the bottom of the bird "see" the surface temperature. Note however that conduction isn't modelled properly because it doesn't involve feedback between the ground and the organism that leads to a change in the ground temperature to a new steady state. It's more as if they keep moving to a new patch of ground of the same temperature.
All the best,
Mike
